lesson.title: Fiesta of Friends: A Week 1 and Week 2 Review
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Today is a fiesta! We're mixing every word from week 1 and week 2 — greetings AND names. Let's celebrate with Sol!
Start like a real conversation: wave and say '¡Hola!' Then ask Sol '¿Cómo te llamas?' and listen for the answer — '¡Me llamo Sol!'
Now it's your turn: tell Sol your name — 'Yo me llamo... (your name)!' Then introduce a friend: 'Mi amigo se llama...' or 'Mi amiga se llama...'

You used words from both weeks together — hola, gracias, me llamo, ¿cómo te llamas?, niño, niña, amigo, and amiga — all in one big fiesta! Wave goodbye and say ¡adiós! — see you next week for counting fun!

objectives: Combine week 1 greeting words and week 2 name-and-friend words in one continuous fiesta routine
Initiate a greeting-and-introduction exchange with hola and ¿cómo te llamas?, and close it with adiós
materialsNeeded: Family members or stuffed animals to complete a 'fiesta' (works fine with just you and your child too)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Gather everyone available (family members, stuffed animals, or just the two of you) into a fiesta circle with Sol.
2. Go around the circle: each person waves and says '¡Hola!', then asks the next person '¿Cómo te llamas?' and listens for 'Me llamo...'.
3. Have each person introduce a partner too: 'Mi amigo se llama...' or 'Mi amiga se llama...'.
4. Mix in a few week-1 favorites: a por favor/gracias exchange, one buenos días stretch, and a silly sí/no question.
5. Sort a leftover niño/niña picture or two if you have them handy, just for fun.
6. Close the fiesta: everyone waves and says '¡Adiós!' to Sol and to each other.
7. Complete the speed-review activity together, celebrating every correct match with a cheer.
differentiationTips: Struggling: skip the full fiesta format and just review a handful of favorite words one-on-one with Sol at your own pace — the goal is joyful recall, not a big production
Ready for more: let your child run the whole fiesta — greeting, asking names, and introducing partners without prompting
This is a celebration lesson — the goal is confident, joyful use of two weeks of words your child already practiced, not teaching anything brand new
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a cumulative spoken review — success looks like your child using a mix of week 1 and week 2 words (hola, gracias, me llamo, ¿cómo te llamas?, niño, niña, amigo, amiga, and more) somewhere in the fiesta, with prompting as needed.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Closes weeks 1 and 2's shared WA-WL-2015.1.1 Interpersonal Communication arc by having the child combine greeting AND self-introduction into one real (if simple) social exchange — the scope-and-sequence's own design for this Day 5, treating the two weeks as one connected conversation skill rather than two separate word lists.
